Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• 40-year-old postpartum woman (4 weeks post-C-section) with sudden shortness of breath at rest, dry cough onset yesterday, pleuritic chest soreness on deep inspiration, and self-measured tachycardia (~120 bpm).  
• Family history of DVT; recent major abdominal surgery; postpartum hypercoagulability.  
• No leg pain, fever, sputum, or chest pain at rest.

Working diagnosis  
Pulmonary embolism (PE) – high suspicion given abrupt dyspnea, tachycardia, recent C-section, postpartum state, and family history of venous thromboembolism.

Other considerations  
• Acute respiratory infection (viral or early pneumonia/bronchitis) – cough present but lacks fever or progressive course.  
• Anxiety/panic attack – stress and palpitations noted but organic risk factors predominate.

Management/Referral  
• Advised immediate hospital evaluation for imaging (CT pulmonary angiogram or V/Q scan) and labs (CBC, D-dimer, ABG) – patient to self-transport with baby.  
• Discussed potential need for anticoagulation if PE confirmed.  
• Advised to withhold further codeine until reviewed in hospital.  
• Offered ambulance; patient declined.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Pulmonary embolism – High likelihood. Sudden dyspnea and tachycardia in a woman 4 weeks post-C-section with family history of DVT and pleuritic discomfort.  
2. Acute respiratory infection (viral/bacterial) – Medium likelihood. New cough and pleuritic soreness could indicate early pneumonia, but abrupt onset and VTE risk factors make this less probable.  
3. Anxiety/panic attack – Medium likelihood. Patient feels very stressed with palpitations; however, objective postoperative VTE risk factors lessen likelihood relative to PE.
